app.process_exited: Process exited: {process}. Please select a process.
menu.backend_frida_tooltip: Default. Injects a Frida agent, full feature set. Does not work with Wine/Proton.
menu.backend_ptrace_tooltip: Uses the ptrace debug API like gdb, without injection. Works with Wine/Proton too. Hooks rewrite the value right after the write (max 4 addresses, no training/caller learning). x86-64 only; needs ptrace_scope=0.
description_dialog.title: Change description
value_dialog.title: Change value
results.title: Scan results
results.add_tooltip: Add selected address to the table below
search.title: Value search
search.auto_type_tooltip: Tries int32, int64, float and double. Smaller types match almost everywhere and have to be chosen explicitly.
search.auto_type_requires_value: Automatic type guessing requires a value or range for the first scan.
search.aligned_tooltip: Only check addresses that are a multiple of the value size (e.g. 4 bytes for int32). Much faster and uses far less memory; applies to the first scan.
search.requires_previous_scan: This scan type compares with the last scan and is only available for the next scan. For the first scan, choose e.g. “Unknown initial value”.
search.tolerance_tooltip: Matches may differ from the search value or change by up to this amount, e.g. 5 with “Increased by 100” for 95 to 105.
search.float_rounding_tooltip: How float and double values are compared with the search value. “Rounded” and “Truncated” use the decimal places entered: 12.3 finds 12.25 to 12.35 or 12.3 to 12.4.
search.close_scan_message: A scan is still running. Cancel it and close the window?
address_table.title: Tracked addresses
address_table.freeze_tooltip: Hold the current value: Hermes writes it back every 100 ms. With a pointer chain this also applies after the program was restarted. Click again to release it.
address_table.freeze_no_value: The current value is not known yet; wait until it is shown in the table.
address_table.remove_candidates_confirm: Remove {count} entries? {candidates} pointer candidates are saved for them and will be removed as well.
address_table.watch_access: Watch reads and writes of this address …
watch.title: Writes to {address}
watch.starting: Attaching to process and setting watchpoints …
watch.already_active: A monitor is already running. Stop it before watching another address.
watch.misaligned: Address must be aligned to {size} bytes for a hardware watchpoint.
watch.still_stopping: The previous monitor is still stopping. Please try again in a moment.
warning.write_failed_message:
Could not write the value to process memory:
{error}
watch.create_hook_tooltip: Hook the write instruction of this row and manipulate the written value
hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.hint: Create hooks from the write monitor window via “Create hook …”.
hooks.training_tooltip: Waiting for a write to the target from the saved code, to find the write site in the newly generated JIT code again. {seen} writes seen so far, {rejected} of them from other code.
hooks.training_paused: Training paused while a write or access watch runs; both use hardware watchpoints and would block each other. Training continues automatically afterwards.
hooks.training_unresolved: Training: the pointer chain does not lead to a target yet (e.g. the game is still in its menu). Once it resolves, the hook waits for the first write.
hooks.training_waiting_slot: Training: all hardware watchpoints are in use; the hook waits until another training has finished.
hooks.saved_for_training: The write instruction is JIT code. The hook is saved with the code around it and, after a restart, found again via its C# method (Mono games) or learned again at the first matching write (status “Training”).
hooks.managed_failed: “{label}” could not be installed via its C# method ({message}); it is trained instead.
hooks.transform_error: Manipulation failed, the original value is kept: {message}
hooks.worker_failed: Connecting to the process for hooks failed: {message}
hooks.label: Description
hooks.not_saved: The write instruction is not inside a module (e.g. JIT code) and the hook has no pointer chain as target; it is not saved. With a pointer chain (start the write watch from an address-list entry with a pointer) it is saved and learned again after a restart.
hooks.caller_depth_hint: How many return addresses identify a caller. The hook remembers the callers that write the target address and, after a restart, only applies to those. More levels help when the player and other objects are changed through the same helper function.
hooks.callers_none: No callers learned yet: let the game change the value once.
hooks.callers_ambiguous: “{label}”: a learned caller also writes other addresses. After a restart the hook would change those too; recreate the hook with more caller levels.
hooks.template_changed: ⚠ The template “{name}” has changed since this hook was created or last updated. The hook still uses its saved copy.
hooks.template_deleted: The template “{name}” has been deleted. The hook still uses its saved copy.
templates.button_tooltip: Create and edit templates for hook manipulations
catalog.button_tooltip: Search the classes and methods of the Mono game (e.g. Unity)
catalog.button_no_mono: Only for games running a Mono runtime (e.g. Unity games using Mono) natively on Linux
catalog.title: C# catalog
catalog.search_placeholder: Search a class or method, e.g. “inventory currency”
catalog.framework_tooltip: Also show mscorlib, System, UnityEngine etc. They are only read when switched on; Mono then loads all their classes.
catalog.reload_tooltip: Read the catalog again, e.g. after the game loaded more assemblies
catalog.copy_tooltip: Copy the signature of the selected method to the clipboard
catalog.monitor_tooltip: Log the calls of the method with arguments and caller (also by double click)
monitor.title: Method monitor
monitor.hint: Logs every call of the monitored C# methods. Mono often builds small methods right into their callers (inlining); the monitor does not see those calls.
monitor.returns_tooltip: Log the return value as well. Frida replaces the return address of every call for that; an exception passing through the method can crash the game.
monitor.status_ended_tooltip: The game freed the method's code (e.g. while exiting); the monitor was removed before.
monitor.dropped: {count} calls not logged (too many at once); the counters include them.
templates.title: Hook templates
templates.name: Name
templates.param_name_invalid: “{name}” is not a valid parameter name (letters, digits, _; not starting with a digit).
templates.param_name_duplicate: The parameter name “{name}” is used twice.
templates.param_choices_required: {name}: Please enter at least one choice.
templates.deleted: Template “{name}” deleted. Existing hooks keep their copy.
templates.delete_confirm: Delete template “{name}”? Existing hooks keep their copy.
templates.unsaved_message: The template has been changed. Save the changes?
templates.test_tooltip: Run the template with sample values, without a game process
templates.test_reset_tooltip: Clear ctx.state; otherwise it is kept between test runs
templates.test_kept: No return value: the game's value ({value}) is kept.
hooks.debug_tooltip: Log every call of this hook in the debug window. Costs time in the game; closing the window ends debug mode.
debug.title: Hook debug
debug.hint: Logs every call of hooks in debug mode and the writes a hook skips. Use ctx.log(…) in a script to add your own output. Select an entry for details.
debug.dropped: {count} dropped by the agent (too many calls)
debug.note_kept: no return value, game value kept
debug.details_placeholder: Select an entry to see details, output and errors.
address_table.pointer_none: No pointer chain: the address is only valid while the program runs. Right-click → “Find pointers …”.
address_table.pointer_tooltip: This chain finds the value again after the program was restarted; it is resolved on every refresh.
address_table.unresolved_tooltip: The pointer chain does not lead to a valid address right now (e.g. still on a loading screen).
address_table.load_failed: Saved addresses could not be resolved: {message}
pointer.title: Pointer scan: {label}
pointer.hint: Searches pointer chains from static memory to this address. The first scan usually finds many candidates. Restart the program (or e.g. reload in the game), find the value again in the scanner – this dialog may stay open –, enter the new address with “Take from scan” and choose “Filter with this address”. After two or three restarts the stable chains remain. The candidates are saved for this entry.
pointer.address_tooltip: Address of the value in the running program; after a restart enter the newly found address.
pointer.depth_tooltip: How many pointers are followed at most. More depth finds more but takes longer.
pointer.offset_tooltip: Largest distance between pointer and target inside an object (e.g. 0x1000).
pointer.filter_tooltip: Keep only the chains that lead to the entered address now
pointer.no_scan: No scan for this entry yet.
pointer.candidates: {count} saved candidates, filtered {rounds}× after a restart.
pointer.max_results_tooltip: Chains are collected shortest first. If the limit is reached, only the longest chains are left out.
pointer.main_module_only_tooltip: Chains have to start in the static memory of the program itself; bases in libraries such as libc are discarded. Turn this off if the data is managed by a library, e.g. a game engine (UnityPlayer.so, libUE4.so).
pointer.limit_reached: The “Max. results” limit was reached: chains of depth {depth} may be incomplete, deeper ones are missing.
pointer.aligned_values_tooltip: Only values that are a multiple of 8 count as pointers. Real pointers to objects almost always are; numbers and bit masks that happen to look like an address usually are not. Turn this off if a chain leads through a pointer into the middle of a structure (e.g. &object->value).
pointer.truncated: The search reached its memory limit: chains up to depth {depth} are complete, longer ones may be missing. Reduce max. offset or depth to find more of them.
pointer.process_exited: The program has exited. This dialog may stay open: restart the program and attach it again with “Select process”, then find the value again in the scanner and filter.
pointer.process_attached: Restarted program attached. Find the value again in the scanner, then “Take from scan” and “Filter with this address”.
pointer.adopt_all_tooltip: Add every candidate to the address list as an entry of its own. After restarting the program the list shows which chains still lead to a sensible value; select the others and remove them.
pointer.adopt_confirm: Add {count} candidates to the address list as entries of their own?
pointer.adopt_limit_confirm: There are {count} candidates. Add the first {limit} (the shortest chains) to the address list as entries of their own? To get fewer candidates, filter after a restart first.
pointer.adopted: {count} candidates added to the address list (chains already in it were skipped).
pointer.entry_missing: The entry of this pointer scan is no longer in the address list.
pointer.found: {count} candidates found and saved. Now restart the program and filter.
pointer.none_found: No pointer chain found. Try a larger depth or offset.
pointer.filtered: {count} of {before} candidates lead to the address (filtered {rounds}×).
pointer.invalid_input: Please enter valid values for address and offset.
pointer.replace_confirm: The new scan replaces the {count} saved candidates. Continue?
hooks.pointer_hint: The hook follows this pointer chain: it only applies to writes of the address the chain currently leads to – also after a restart and when the game allocates the object anew.
debug.skipped_pointer: skipped: pointer chain leads nowhere right now
pointer.static: This address is static ({chain}): it lies in the program's own data and is found again after a restart without a pointer scan.
pointer.none_found_static: No pointer chain found – none needed: the address is static (see above).
pointer.from_scan_tooltip: Enter the address of the result selected in the scanner. The dialog may stay open meanwhile.
pointer.from_scan_none: Select a result in the scanner first; the dialog may stay open meanwhile.
hooks.script_hint: A JavaScript function that runs inside the target process after every write. Available are e.g. ctx.old, ctx.new, ctx.delta, ctx.params, ctx.state (kept between calls) and ctx.log(…) for output in the debug window. The return value is stored; undefined keeps the game's value.
memview.title: Memory viewer
memview.button_tooltip: View the process memory as a hex dump
memview.live_tooltip: Read the shown memory twice per second; changed bytes are highlighted for a moment.
memview.no_selection: Select a byte to see its values.
memview.process_exited: The program has exited. Once a process is attached, the viewer shows its memory.
